title: Steel Mount Link and Bushed Attachment at the Auxiliary Power Unit Aft Mount

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: First answer to auxiliary power unit aft mount wear: a steel mount link in place of the original aluminium item, with a replaceable bush at both ends so that wear is taken by a serviceable part rather than by the link itself.

sections.reason: Elongation of the aft mount link bores was found on nineteen aircraft at the first heavy check, well inside the interval the design assumed. The original link is aluminium with an integral bore, so any wear is wear of a structural part and the only remedy is link replacement. Operators with high auxiliary power unit utilisation were replacing links at every heavy check. The wear itself is not a safety issue at the rates observed, because the mount is redundant, but the cost and the downtime were not acceptable and there was no inspection that could distinguish acceptable wear from the beginning of a problem.
sections.description: The aft mount link D4910124356332 is replaced by a steel item of the same length and the same attachment geometry, and a replaceable bush is introduced at both ends. The firewall panel D4910122171974 is modified locally to clear the slightly larger link boss. The bracket D4910125048089 that carries the aft attachment is renewed with a reamed bore to the new bush outside diameter. The retaining hardware XAN342388-19 is replaced at both ends. Wiring at FIN 2PB7 and the tube support at FIN 2PA8 are disturbed for access and reinstated unchanged. Work is in the tail cone in zones 313 and 325 with the auxiliary power unit access doors open and the aft heat shield dropped. The change is detailed on drawing D49101239814. The auxiliary power unit itself, its forward mounts and its exhaust are unchanged.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 6.8 kg per aircraft, well aft of the reference station, giving a centre-of-gravity shift of approximately 0.04 per cent mean aerodynamic chord which is accounted for in the weight and balance amendment. No electrical effect. The steel link is not interchangeable with the aluminium item because the bracket bore is reamed to a different size. Dispatch is unchanged. The mount inspection remains at the same interval but becomes a bush measurement rather than a link measurement, which is a shop-floor task rather than a structural assessment.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN T00122 in September 2016. Retrofit through the associated service bulletin, about one and a half shifts with the tail cone open and the aft heat shield removed. The heat shield removal is the largest part of the elapsed time.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft of reference station, CG shift approximately 0.04 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN T00122, no line stoppage
